L.title: Adding expressions: match up like terms
L.why: Only like terms combine: m-terms with m-terms, numbers with numbers. Every term keeps its own sign.

steps: Pair the like terms: (2/3)m with (5/6)m, and 4 with −7.

watch: Count both m-terms, not just one.
Keep each sign: the −7 stays negative.
A number never joins an m-term: (3/2)m − 3 is finished.

L.title: Adding decimal terms: add the numbers in front
L.why: 0.4x + 1.6x means 0.4 of x plus 1.6 of x, which is 2x. Add the coefficients; the x stays the same.

practice.change: the coefficients make a whole number

watch: Add the coefficients, don't multiply them: 0.4 × 1.6 = 0.64 has nothing to do with it.
An x-term and a number stay separate: 2x − 0.5 does not become 1.5x.
Check the sign of the number: 2 + (−2.5) = −0.5.

L.title: The missing expression: undo it with subtraction
L.why: If A − ? = B, then ? = A − B, just like 10 − ? = 7 means ? = 10 − 7. Subtracting a negative adds.

practice.change: a plus sign: now ? = right side − left part

watch: Two minuses make a plus: 2/3 − (−3/8) = 2/3 + 3/8.
Start with the left expression: ? = left − right. Right − left flips every sign.

L.title: Subtracting a group: the minus reaches every term
L.why: −(a + b) = −a − b. Subtracting a whole group subtracts each term in it, so every sign in the second group flips.

steps: Flip every sign in the second group: (5/2)x − 3 − (1/2)x − 6.

watch: Flip both signs in the second group: −((7/3)x + 4) = −(7/3)x − 4.
Subtract in order, first minus second: 4/3 − 7/3 = −1, so −x.
Subtracting a group is not adding it.

L.title: From a situation: write it whole, then simplify
L.why: Write the full expression with parentheses first, then distribute and combine. A rectangle's perimeter is 2(length) + 2(width).

example.prompt: A rectangle is (3x + 1.5) cm long and ((1/2)x − 1) cm wide. Write and simplify its perimeter.

turn.prompt: A rectangle is (2x − 0.5) ft long and ((3/2)x + 4) ft wide. Write and simplify its perimeter.

practice.prompt: A square has sides of (x + 2.5) inches. Write and simplify its perimeter.
A triangle has sides of (2x + 1), (x − 3) and ((1/2)x + 4) meters. Write and simplify its perimeter.
Tickets cost (x + 4.5) dollars each. Kim buys 3 tickets and uses a $5 coupon. Write and simplify her total.

watch: Perimeter is all four sides: 2(length) + 2(width), not length + width once.
Double every term: 2(x − 2) = 2x − 4.
Keep the sign: −4, not +4.

L.title: Distributing a fraction: multiply every term
L.why: a(b + c) = ab + ac. The number outside multiplies each term inside. It never adds.

practice.change: the number doesn't come out whole

watch: Multiply, don't add: (5/4)(12x) is 15x, not (12 + 5/4)x.
Both terms get multiplied: 15x + 25, not 15x + 20.
15x + 25 does not become 40x: unlike terms stay apart.

L.title: Spot the error: multiply both terms, then stop
L.why: Two slips cause most wrong answers: multiplying only the first term, then adding an x-term to a number. An answer like 16x + 16 is finished.

example.prompt: A student rewrote (3/2)(4x + 6) as 12x. What is the correct expression?
steps: Slip 1: the student multiplied only 4x, getting 6x + 6.
Slip 2: then added 6x and 6 as if they were like terms: 12x.

turn.prompt: A student rewrote (5/3)(6x + 3) as 13x. What is the correct expression?
steps: The student kept the 3 (10x + 3), then added: 13x.

practice.prompt: A student rewrote 2.5(4x + 2) as 12x. Correct it.
A student rewrote (1/2)(8x − 6) as 4x − 6. Correct it.
A student rewrote (3/4)(8x + 4) as (35/4)x + 19/4. Correct it.

watch: Slip 1: only the first term gets multiplied.
Slip 2: an x-term plus a number turned into one x-term.
Slip 3: the fraction was added to each term instead of multiplied.

L.title: Distributing a decimal: same rule, careful multiplying
L.why: 1.5(6x − 2) means 1.5 × 6x and 1.5 × (−2). The minus stays with the 2.

practice.change: a negative outside: both signs flip

watch: Multiply, don't add: 1.5 + 6 = 7.5 is the wrong move.
Multiply the second term too, sign and all: 1.5 × (−2) = −3.
9x − 3 has two unlike terms; it does not shrink to 6x.

L.title: Equivalent or not: simplify both, then compare
L.why: Two expressions are equivalent when they simplify to the same thing: the same x-coefficient and the same number. Looking alike is not enough.
watch: Simplify before deciding; don't judge by looks.
"Both have an x-term and a number" does not make them equal.
Multiply both terms: 2.5(8x − 2) = 20x − 5, not 20x − 2.

L.title: A negative outside the parentheses: flip every sign inside
L.why: −(3/4)(4x − 4) multiplies both terms by −3/4: −3x and +3. A negative times a negative is positive.

steps: Same x-term and same number, so they are equivalent.

watch: A negative times a negative is positive: −(3/4)(−4) = +3, not −3.
The same number at the end is not enough; the x-terms must match too.

L.title: Reading a graph: the circle and the arrow
L.why: Open circle: the boundary is not included (< or >). Closed circle: it is included (≤ or ≥). Shading to the left means less than; to the right, greater than.

example.prompt: Which inequality has the solution shown?   4x ≥ −12  ·  4x > −12  ·  x + 4 ≥ −12  ·  4x ≤ −12
steps: The graph shows x ≥ −3: closed circle at −3, shaded right.
4x > −12 has an open circle; x + 4 ≥ −12 has boundary −16; 4x ≤ −12 shades left.

turn.prompt: Which inequality has the solution shown?   1.5x ≤ 7.5  ·  1.5x < 7.5  ·  x + 1.5 < 7.5  ·  1.5x > 7.5
steps: The graph shows x < 5: open circle at 5, shaded left.

practice.prompt: Write the inequality the graph shows.
Write the inequality the graph shows.
Does 0.5x ≤ 3 match the graph? Does x − 0.5 ≤ 3?
practice.answer: 0.5x ≤ 3 does (x ≤ 6). x − 0.5 ≤ 3 gives x ≤ 3.5, so it does not.

watch: An open circle means < or >: the number itself is not a solution.
Solve each choice to find its boundary: x + 2.5 < 20 gives 17.5, not 8.
Shading to the left means less than.

L.title: Adding or subtracting: the symbol stays put
L.why: Adding or subtracting the same number on both sides never flips the inequality. Only multiplying or dividing by a negative does that.

practice.change: the variable is on the right

watch: Adding or subtracting never flips the symbol.
Undo −3 by adding 3: −6.9 + 3 = −3.9.
−6.9 + 3 is still negative: picture the number line.

L.title: Dividing by a negative flips the symbol
L.why: −2 < 3, but multiply both by −1 and you get 2 > −3. Multiplying or dividing by a negative reverses the order, so the symbol flips.

steps: Divide both sides by −2 and flip ≥ to ≤.
x ≤ −3.5: closed circle at −3.5, shaded left.

turn.answer: w > −4: open circle at −4, shaded right.

practice.answer: p < −4: open circle at −4, shaded left
q ≥ 4: closed circle at 4, shaded right
r < −4: open circle at −4, shaded left. No flip.

watch: Forgetting the flip puts the shading on the wrong side.
> and < get open circles.

L.title: Words to an inequality: product, sum, at least, at most
L.why: Translate piece by piece. "The product of x and −0.5" is −0.5x. "At least" means ≥ and "at most" means ≤.

example.prompt: The product of a number x and −4 is at least 10. What are the possible values of x?
steps: Check x = −3: −4(−3) = 12, and 12 is at least 10.

turn.prompt: The product of a number y and −0.5 is greater than 3. What are the possible values of y?

practice.prompt: A number n divided by 3 is at most 4.
The sum of a number x and 2.5 is less than −1.
The product of −2 and a number z is at most −9.

watch: Divide to undo multiplying: x > 2.5 came from multiplying −5 by −0.5.
Dividing by a negative flips the symbol: x < 10 forgot to.
"At least" includes the number: ≥.

L.title: Matching a graph: solve every choice, check three things
L.why: Solve each choice, then compare three things with the graph: the boundary number, open or closed, and the direction.

example.prompt: The graph shows the solution of one choice. Which?   (a) x + 2 ≤ 5   (b) −2x ≤ −6   (c) x/3 < 1   (d) x − 1 ≤ 3
steps: The graph: closed circle at 3, shaded left, so x ≤ 3.
(b) x ≥ 3: wrong direction.  (c) x < 3: open circle.  (d) x ≤ 4: wrong boundary.

turn.prompt: Which matches the graph?   (a) −3x < 3   (b) x + 4 ≥ 3   (c) x/2 > −1   (d) −x > 1
steps: The graph: open circle at −1, shaded right, so x > −1.
(b) x ≥ −1: closed circle.  (c) x > −2: wrong boundary.  (d) x < −1: wrong direction.

practice.prompt: Solve −0.5x ≥ 2. Give the boundary, open or closed, and direction.
Solve x − 3.5 > −1.5. Boundary, open or closed, direction?
Solve x/(−2) < 1.5. Boundary, open or closed, direction?

watch: Check all three: boundary, circle, direction.
Don't stop at the first choice with the right number.

L.title: Fee plus rate: write it, then undo in reverse order
L.why: Total = one-time fee + rate × number. The rate goes with the variable; the fee stands alone. Undo the fee first (subtract), then the rate (divide).

example.prompt: A bowling alley charges $4.00 for shoes plus $5.50 for each game. Lena paid $26.00. How many games did she bowl?

turn.prompt: A taxi charges $3.00 plus $2.25 per mile. The ride cost $16.50. How many miles?

practice.prompt: A gym charges $35 to join plus $18 per month. Sam has paid $125. How many months?
A plumber charges $45 for the visit plus $30 per hour. The bill was $150. How many hours?
A phone costs $120 up front plus $15.50 a month. Ana has paid $213 in all. How many months?

watch: The rate goes with the variable (12.5h); the fee stands alone (+ 25).
Undo + 25 by subtracting 25, not adding it.
Check by putting the answer back into the story.

L.title: Equations with parentheses: undo the outside first
L.why: In 1.5(h + 1.6) = −0.6, the whole group (h + 1.6) is multiplied by 1.5. Undo that first by dividing, then undo the + 1.6.

steps: Or distribute first: 2.5k − 3 = −4, so 2.5k = −1 and k = −0.4.

watch: Divide by the number in front; don't multiply.
Then undo + 1.6 by subtracting: −0.4 − 1.6 = −2.
If you distribute instead, multiply both terms: 1.5h + 2.4.

L.title: Groups: when the change happens to each one
L.why: If each of 3 students gets $5 more, each now has (s + 5), and together they have 3(s + 5). Writing 3s + 5 would give out only one $5.

example.prompt: Four friends each paid t dollars for a ticket plus $2.50 for a snack. They spent $46 in all. Find t.

turn.prompt: Five boxes each held b books. Then 3 books were taken out of each box. Now there are 60 books. Find b.

practice.prompt: Six bags each held p pounds of rice. Then 0.5 pound was taken out of each. Now the bags hold 21 pounds in all. Find p.
Three tables each seat s people. Two more chairs are added to each table, and now 24 people can sit. Find s.

watch: The $5 goes to each student: 3(s + 5), not 3s + 5.
Finish the job: s + 5 = 35 means s = 30, not 35.
"Decreased" or "taken out" means subtract inside the parentheses.

L.title: Fraction equations: add, then use the reciprocal
L.why: Undo − 4 by adding 4. Then (2/3)g means 2/3 of g: undo it by multiplying by 3/2, which is the same as dividing by 2/3.

practice.change: the answer is a mixed number

watch: Undo (2/3)g by multiplying by 3/2, not by 2/3.

L.title: Two-part problems: solve, then answer the real question
L.why: Solve for the unknown first, then use it. Underline what is asked: which one, and by how much?

example.prompt: Pool A charges $6.50 per visit. Eli used a $10 coupon and paid $55 in all. Pool B charges $7.25 per visit and takes no coupons. For the same number of visits, which pool costs less, and by how much?

turn.prompt: Store A sells notebooks for $3.40 each. Ty used a $5 coupon and paid $29. Store B sells them for $3.15 each, no coupons. For the same number of notebooks, which store costs less, and by how much?

practice.prompt: A class paid $15 for a bus plus $4.50 per student. The total was $123. How many students went?
Plan A costs $12.50 a month with $20 off the total. Mia paid $130. Plan B costs $11 a month, nothing off. For the same months, which costs less, and by how much?

watch: Put the coupon in the equation: 24.5n − 35 = 185.5.
Don't stop at n = 9: answer which gym and how much.
Compare totals, not monthly prices.

levels: I can write and simplify an expression from a real-world situation.
Mia earns (3x + 5) dollars on Saturday and (2.5x − 1) dollars on Sunday. Her total is 5.5x + 4 dollars.
I can add and subtract linear expressions with rational coefficients.
I can combine like terms with integer coefficients.

C-AR.1.2.goal: I can tell whether two expressions are equivalent.
levels: I can justify equivalence using properties of operations, including factoring.
12x + 18 = 6(2x + 3) by the distributive property: 6 · 2x = 12x and 6 · 3 = 18.
I can decide whether two linear expressions are equivalent and rewrite one as the other.
2(3x − 1) + x and 7x − 2: 6x − 2 + x = 7x − 2, so they are equivalent.
I can use the distributive property on a simple expression.
I need help to start this.
Start here: multiply the number outside by each term inside.

C-AR.2.1.goal: I can write and solve one-step inequalities and graph the solutions.
levels: I can write an inequality from a real-world situation, solve it, and interpret the solution.
Each video uses 0.75 GB and Ana has 4.5 GB left: 0.75v ≤ 4.5, so v ≤ 6. She can watch at most 6 videos.
I can solve a one-step inequality, including with negative numbers, and graph the solution.
−3x < 12 → x > −4 (divide by −3 and flip)
I can graph an inequality on a number line.
x ≥ −2: closed circle at −2, shaded right
I need help to start this.
Start here: open circle means not included; closed circle means included.

C-AR.2.2.goal: I can write and solve two-step equations.
levels: I can write a two-step equation from a real-world context, solve it, and check the answer.
A gym charges $20 to join plus $15 a month. Ana paid $95: 15m + 20 = 95, so m = 5. Check: 15(5) + 20 = 95.
I can solve a two-step equation, including with rational numbers or the distributive property.
I can solve a one-step equation.
I need help to start this.
Start here: undo in reverse order. Add or subtract first, then multiply or divide.
